🇲🇽🎓 <u>UAM Strike: 4.9 Million Pesos for Officials' Cars, Students Ask for Food</u>

The strike at the Metropolitan Autonomous University (UAM) in Mexico City is nearing one month across all five campuses. It began on October 20 at the Cuajimalpa campus, after officials spent 4,922,390 pesos on six electric cars. Students have filed 446 demands covering canteens, scholarships, lab supplies, water, toilets, teaching staff and security. An emergency session of the Academic College on November 16 lasted 11 hours and 52 minutes and ended without a deal. One protest sign read: "Hunger for students, cars for the authorities."

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>Morena's 2027 Slate: The Green Party Quietly Takes Three States</u>

While pundits watched the PT, the Partido Verde quietly secured three governor candidacies, according to an analysis in Contralínea. Morena gave it Nayarit, with Jasmine Bugarín, a senator who used to be in the PRI. It also gave it Baja California Sur, with Manuel Cota, son of former governor Leonel Cota. In San Luis Potosí, Morena's weak pick likely clears the way for Ruth González, the wife of Governor Ricardo Gallardo. The author's verdict is that the pragmatism of bringing in PRI and PAN defectors "has become an institutionalized practice."

🇲🇽📊 <u>17.3 Million Out of Poverty, No Growth Boom Required</u>

According to the World Bank, 17.3 million Mexicans left poverty between 2018 and 2026, and more than 20 million have done so since the 2020 pandemic peak. Writing in Contralínea, Josafat Hernández argues this breaks "the fetishism of economic growth," the trickle-down dogma that wellbeing can't rise without fast GDP growth. Mexico raised wages and redistributed instead of waiting for crumbs. Under the old model, real wages fell nearly 89% between 1987 and 2014, according to UNAM's Center for Multidisciplinary Analysis.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN's Azcapotzalco: 46 Million Pesos Unaccounted For</u>

Mexico's Federal Audit Office (ASF) has ordered an investigation into officials from PAN mayor Margarita Saldaña's administration in Azcapotzalco, Mexico City. At issue is an alleged loss of more than 46 million pesos in 2024 contracts whose spending could not be verified. The ASF flagged eight companies, including Gluckill SA, which held a contract worth more than 26 million pesos and which current mayor Nancy Núñez links to a former purchasing director. An earlier ASF audit had already found 39 million pesos undocumented under Saldaña in 2021.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Rosario Robles Loses Again: Court Upholds Her Ban From Public Office</u>

Mexico's Federal Administrative Justice Tribunal (TFJA) unanimously upheld a one-year ban on Rosario Robles, Peña Nieto's social development secretary, for leaving a bank account off her asset declarations. Her lawyers argued she was being tried twice for the same offense, and the magistrates threw that out. The ban was originally 10 years in 2019 and was cut to one year in 2023. It is a separate case from the Estafa Maestra, in which she was acquitted.

🇲🇽💵 <u>The Fed Sneezes, the Peso Pays: 41 Centavos Gone in One Session</u>

The peso lost 41 centavos against the dollar Wednesday — more than 2%, per El Economista — from Tuesday's Banxico close of 18.43. Nothing changed in Mexico: the slide tracked a global dollar rally as markets priced a December Fed hike at 97.3% odds after Fed governor Christopher Waller called for a 50-basis-point increase to fight US inflation. Monex: "The peso aligns with most currencies globally, which are retreating against the US dollar."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"I'm Going to Blow Her Up": Cerimedo's Plan for Mexico's Presidential Race</u>

Nadia Beller, the Bolivian lawyer who found refuge in Mexico, told Carmen Aristegui that Argentine far-right consultant Fernando Cerimedo vowed to intervene in Mexico's next presidential election to bring down Claudia Sheinbaum: "La voy a reventar." According to Beller, he was furious over Sheinbaum's clash with Spanish propagandist Javier Negre of La Derecha Diario. Beller survived being shot at in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, on August 17 and names Cerimedo as the mastermind.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Segob: Organized Crime Paid Protesters to Block Santa Fe</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez confirmed federal authorities are investigating payments by a criminal group — allegedly ordered by an inmate of Federal Prison No. 4 in Nayarit — to people who blocked Santa Fe demanding "better conditions" for prisoners. Both those who paid and those who organized will be investigated. "It cannot be that they are paying people to block roads, especially people totally linked to organized crime."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The Old Bosses of the INE Now Demand "Consensus" — As the ASF Audits Their Years</u>

José Woldenberg, Luis Carlos Ugalde, Leonardo Valdés and Lorenzo Córdova — four former heads of IFE/INE — asked the Chamber of Deputies to name the new INE president "by consensus" and to rethink the makeup of the General Council. The call lands as the ASF prepares a review of INE procurement from 2000 to 2025, the exact span of their tenures, and after the INE itself filed an FGR complaint over electoral-materials contracts. Ugalde joined by video from Boston, where he has lived for a year and a half.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>400-Meter Huachicol Tunnel Found Under Mexico City, Blocks from the Airport</u>

Crews repairing a sinkhole in Venustiano Carranza's colonia 20 de Noviembre found a hose running two blocks underground. It led to a tunnel of more than 400 meters feeding a clandestine diesel tap inside a house on Calle Cerámica, a few blocks from Circuito Interior and the AICM. Pemex Strategic Safeguarding, the Guardia Nacional and CDMX police sealed the site, and the FGR opens a case for theft of fuel "considered the nation's patrimony."
